# Project Governance 4.5.1

Completed or failed workflows can finish original resource cleanup through a public owner command.
It preserves original run identities, complete lease generations, runtime readers, failure receipts
and clocks. Positive process-start evidence also allows terminal reader recovery after PID reuse.
No live owner is stopped and no automatic stage replay is introduced.

Qualified iOS observation/simulator and Android app-session closure retain actual device, app and
local-lock custody. Android observation handles complete process names and attributes isolated
services to the selected package UID before deciding absence. Borrowed targets remain running;
owned-emulator closure requires original boot ownership and full shutdown evidence.
New submissions using `android:` or `app:` claims must declare their explicit app-session lifetime;
older bound runs retain their original contracts. Update project recipe declarations deliberately.

A separately selected, explicit local-host recovery can use fresh host and real-mutex observations
when an original failed local report omitted its historical process join. This deliberate exception
requires the original exact scope, recorded authority decision and historical mutex mapping. It is
not an automatic fallback: the normal local-host overlap rule remains enforced, and the new receipt
records the missing historical join. Never rewrite old reports or convert a failed run into success.

The demand-driven JEV behavior from 4.5.0 remains intact. Publication does not install this release
into any project, release its held resources, change model/provider permissions or establish savings.
Actual recovery belongs to the original owner after explicit admission; device proof and accepted
application outcomes remain separate from synthetic release qualification.
